chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then when they fall down, eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The contented is the one who is content with whatever you give him; and the mu'tarr is the one who passes by you; and the beggar is the one who asks you with his hand; and the ba'is is the poor one.'

key_terms.الْمُعْتَرُّ: The one who passes by / is present

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the contented and the beggar in the verse about sacrificial animals?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi offers a nuanced exegetical breakdown of Al-Hajj 22:36, clarifying the distinct social categories of recipients for sacrificial meat. It defines the 'mu'tarr' not merely as a beggar, but specifically as one who passes by or is present, distinguishing them from the 'qani' (contented) and the 'ba'is' (poor), thereby guiding the practical distribution of charity in Shia jurisprudence.
